rubric_items.reason: Every changed part (CO-1 to CO-5, EP-1 to EP-3) has a test. Some story ACs are mapped to tests but not exercised: S-3 AC1/AC2 ordering, S-1 AC4 no period picker, and S-2 AC2 (Scheduled and Cancelled only) at the API.
API tests use exact toEqual on visitSummary and check status codes. The web REQ-7/REQ-9 test only checks that elements exist (toBeTruthy), so it cannot catch a changed order or content.
Good edge cases: past unclosed Scheduled, latest Cancelled, other patient, all time, zero. The only error test is GET 404; the changed POST and PATCH endpoints have no error-path test.
Uses Vitest+Supertest with its own throwaway DB and a fixed clock, and Vitest+jsdom+Testing Library on the web side. Test names start with HMS-5 REQ-n, as existing tests in test-layout do.
Reports no counts or coverage. It defers results to the verifier, and checks.json shows coverage skipped (exit 78), which matches C5.

findings.text: EP-2 (POST) and EP-3 (PATCH) changed, but neither has an error-path test. The only error test is GET /api/patients/9999 returning 404. Rubric trigger: changed endpoint without an error-path test.

request(app).get('/api/patients/9999')

findings.suggested_fix: Add HMS-5 tests: PATCH on an unknown patient still returns 404, and POST with invalid fields is still rejected with field errors.

findings.text: The artifact says the web tests cover S-3 AC1, but the fixture has one appointment and the test checks only that a link exists, so 'upcoming first, then past' is never tested. S-3 AC2 has no test.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixture with one upcoming and one past appointment and assert row order (S-3 AC1). Add a past-only case (S-3 AC2), or drop the AC1 mapping.
